title: Ollama
description: A local model runtime that downloads and runs open-weight models on a laptop behind a simple CLI and API, built on llama.cpp.
capabilityNote: Runs quantised open-weight models locally; later added a desktop app (v0.10, Jul 2025) and an MLX backend on Macs.

majorUpdates.title: Desktop app (v0.10)
majorUpdates.summary: A desktop app alongside the CLI.

title: Stack Overflow's Q&A decline
description: Public question volume on Stack Overflow fell from about 200,000 a month at its 2014 peak to 1,072 in June 2026 as developers moved to chat assistants and coding agents.
capabilityNote: The company survives in smaller form on enterprise products and AI data-licensing deals.

sources.title: DevClass: dramatic drop in Stack Overflow questions
The New Stack: Stack Overflow's plan to survive

title: Radiologists and AI
description: After deep learning matched specialists on some image-reading benchmarks, radiology became the standard example of a job AI would replace. Demand for radiologists kept rising instead.
capabilityNote: Average radiologist pay reached $571K in 2025, with 7,469 active radiology job postings in May 2026 and caseload up about 25% from 2018 to early 2025.

sources.title: Fortune: radiologist salaries up to $571K, demand growing

title: Entry-level hiring in AI-exposed jobs
description: As coding agents spread, programming did not disappear, but entry-level hiring weakened: new-grad hiring at the 15 largest tech firms fell more than 50% from 2019.
capabilityNote: Stanford Digital Economy Lab research finds employment of young workers in the most AI-exposed occupations below trend, with no economy-wide displacement.

sources.title: Stanford Digital Economy Lab: canaries in the coal mine

title: AI and white-collar jobs
description: Large employers began citing generative AI in workforce plans. Cuts were real at some firms, but how much AI caused them is disputed, and several companies walked back AI-first staffing claims.
capabilityNote: The 18 occupations the BLS flagged as AI-exposed fell 0.2% (May 2024–May 2025) while total US employment rose 0.8%. Amazon cut about 30,000 corporate jobs across late 2025 and early 2026.

sources.title: PBS: Amazon lays off 14,000 corporate employees

title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
description: Combined a language model with a retriever over a document index so answers can draw on, and cite, external text. It became the default pattern for grounding LLM apps in 2023.
capabilityNote: Retrieval later moved into agentic search and tool use rather than disappearing; long context replaced the mandatory vector database for some uses.

sources.title: Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
LightOn: retrieval in the age of agents

title: Vector databases
description: Databases for embedding search boomed as the storage layer for RAG. The category commoditised as vector search became a feature of Postgres, Elastic, MongoDB and the cloud providers.
capabilityNote: Pinecone explored a sale in 2025 and named a new CEO in September 2025, staying independent into 2026.

sources.title: VentureBeat: the vector database story two years later

title: Jev (TypeSafe AI)
description: A “System One” decision model that returns typed choices, scores and calibrated probabilities instead of free text, aimed at high-volume classification and routing. TypeSafe AI came out of stealth with a $40M seed.
capabilityNote: Priced at $0.042 per 1M input tokens with output free (TypeSafe docs). TypeSafe's "193.6x faster, 444.6x cheaper" figures are vendor-reported and not independently replicated. Jev 1.14 (14 October) added Box questions.

sources.title: A deep dive into Jev, TypeSafe's System One model
What Is Jev? Inside TypeSafe's Decision-Only AI Model

title: Mem0
description: A memory layer for AI agents that extracts, stores, and recalls facts across sessions behind a drop-in API, evolving out of Embedchain.
capabilityNote: Positioned as the memory layer for agents; combines an open-source core with a hosted memory graph.

sources.title: Mem0: The Memory Layer for AI Agents

title: Welcome to the Era of Experience
description: David Silver and Richard Sutton's foundational essay arguing that frontier AI is transitioning from learning on static human data to self-improving through direct environment interaction and experience.
capabilityNote: Framed the post-pretraining research agenda around trial-and-error experience as the path beyond human imitation.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
description: Anthropic's engineering guide establishing context engineering as the core discipline for production agents, treating context as a scarce budget requiring active curation rather than unbounded prompt growth.
capabilityNote: Crystallized the industry shift from prompt crafting to tool-mediated context management and sub-agent compaction.

sources.title: Anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents

title: Strix
description: An open-source AI penetration testing agent designed to autonomously uncover and remediate web application security vulnerabilities.
capabilityNote: Reached over 66,000 GitHub stars, reflecting the rapid growth of autonomous offensive and defensive security harnesses.

title: Pi (pi-mono)
description: Mario Zechner's self-extensible AI coding agent toolkit and monorepo featuring a unified LLM API, agent loop, interactive TUI, and CLI harness.
capabilityNote: Crossed 110k stars as a hacker favorite; reached version 1.0 in October 2026 with Pi Durable for resilient multi-hour sessions.

majorUpdates.title: Pi 1.0
majorUpdates.summary: Full 1.0 release stabilizing the extensible agent loop and TUI.

majorUpdates.title: Pi Durable
majorUpdates.summary: Durable checkpointing and background task execution for long-running workflows.

title: MiroFish
description: A swarm intelligence prediction engine using coordinated multi-agent simulation sandboxes to forecast complex events and macro scenarios.
capabilityNote: Gained over 75,000 GitHub stars, pioneering community-driven synthetic prediction swarms and multi-agent consensus dynamics.

title: Edge0
description: An edge-focused AI organization building on-device MoE language models and compact speech systems designed to run directly on consumer-tier silicon.
capabilityNote: Developed the ARK-ASR, Audio8 TTS series, and lightweight 8B/35B-A3B edge MoE architectures to bypass reliance on cloud inference.

title: OpenViking
description: ByteDance Volcengine's self-evolving context database for AI agents, uniting episodic agent memory, persistent RAG knowledge, and operational skills in one engine.
capabilityNote: Quickly crossed 39,000 stars, establishing dedicated memory and state management plugins across major agent coding harnesses.

title: cmux
description: A Ghostty-based macOS terminal environment engineered specifically for multiplexing and orchestrating concurrent AI coding agent sessions with vertical tabs and status alerts.
capabilityNote: A spiritual successor to tmux adapted for the agentic era, resolving the ergonomics of tracking multiple autonomous coding agents in parallel.

title: Oh My Agent
description: A harness enhancement and skills toolkit providing mechanical verification, stop-hook gates, and guardrails for terminal coding agents.
capabilityNote: Part of the broader 'oh-my-*' harness modularization wave alongside oh-my-codex, shifting emphasis toward deterministic runtime constraints.

title: Awesome AI Agent Papers
description: A community-curated collection tracking landmark research papers in agent architectures, tool use, long-horizon evaluation, and cognitive frameworks.
capabilityNote: Serves as a canonical index filtering high-signal empirical publications amidst exponential growth in agent academic preprints.

title: Soup
description: A single-YAML LLM fine-tuning framework implementing layer streaming to train 8B models on consumer hardware with as little as 4 GB of VRAM.
capabilityNote: Demonstrated that low-resource layer-by-layer optimization can democratize model adaptation on commodity laptops.

title: Paperclip
description: An open-source workspace application for managing fleets of AI agents at work, orchestrating tasks, reviews, and delegation across human and synthetic team members.
capabilityNote: Surged past 96,000 GitHub stars within months, pioneering corporate agent orchestration and organization modeling.

title: OpenCLI
description: A developer tool that turns authenticated web sessions into CLI endpoints, enabling AI agents to drive web services directly through existing browser credentials.
capabilityNote: Achieved nearly 30,000 GitHub stars by offering zero-config automation across dozens of web platforms without fragile API mocking.

title: Open Design
description: An open-source, local-first UI design agent and harness plugin designed as an open alternative to proprietary visual coding assistants.
capabilityNote: Reached nearly 100,000 stars on GitHub, bridging code-generation harnesses with real-time visual canvas iteration.

title: Colibri
description: A pure-C, dependency-free local inference engine designed to execute frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on consumer hardware by streaming inactive experts directly from disk.
capabilityNote: Gained 39,000 stars by making massive MoE architectures viable on low-RAM workstations with minimal throughput degradation.

title: Google ARTEMIS
description: Google's open-source framework transforming natural language instructions into multi-step Android device automation, featuring MCP integration for IDEs and diagnostic logging.
capabilityNote: Reported 99%+ completion on Google Research's AndroidWorld benchmark, bridging coding IDEs with native mobile OS execution.

title: Ox Alpha model unmasking
description: Community model forensics publicly demonstrated that OpenCode's free, unbranded 'ox-alpha' provider route was backed by Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash weights.
capabilityNote: High-profile case of black-box model fingerprinting in developer tooling, illustrating how labs use free proxy tiers to seed adoption.

sources.title: Reproducible black-box model forensics for OpenCode Ox Alpha

title: Livenerf
description: An automated evaluation harness designed to continuously detect post-launch degradation, safety-prompt regressions, and capacity nerfing in hosted frontier LLMs.
capabilityNote: Turned persistent community speculation ('has Opus 5.5 been nerfed?') into quantifiable, continuously published benchmark charts.

title: Ember-1
description: Fireworks Research's specialized reasoning model distilled from Kimi K3, trained to cut unnecessary chain-of-thought tokens by 40% while preserving answer quality.
capabilityNote: Pioneered explicit token-efficiency distillation to make agentic reasoning traces economically viable at massive scale.

title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
description: The second model in Anthropic's Claude 5.5 generation, offering a 30%+ speed increase and 30% lower operating cost while achieving 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.
capabilityNote: Demonstrated dramatic improvement on long-horizon visual agent tasks, including becoming the first model to complete Pokémon Red purely from screen pixels.

title: GPT-6.1 Sol
description: OpenAI's major efficiency upgrade to GPT-6 Sol, approaching GPT-6 Astra benchmark performance on software engineering at one-fifth the inference cost.
capabilityNote: Aggressively dropped cached token pricing to $0.10 per million tokens, targeting high-context agent execution loops.

title: ChatGPT Dots
description: Always-on proactive personal agents introduced at OpenAI DevDay 2026, running background tasks on persistent dedicated compute powered by GPT-6 Astra.
capabilityNote: Marked OpenAI's shift from interactive conversational bots to autonomous, persistent digital workers with permissioned tool access.

title: GLM-5.3 and emergent cyber capabilities
description: Anthropic's red-team research demonstrating that open-weight model GLM-5.3 autonomously developed full control-flow hijacks in 4% of binary exploitation benchmarks.
capabilityNote: Marked the first documented empirical threshold where non-frontier open weights achieved automated software exploitation capabilities previously exclusive to top-tier closed models.

sources.title: Anthropic: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities

title: Agent worms via shared package caches
description: Matthew Green's analysis demonstrating that sandbox isolation fails to contain rogue agents when shared package caches and inter-agent communication channels permit persistent self-propagating payloads.
capabilityNote: Demonstrated the theoretical and practical reality of self-replicating multi-agent malware spreading across autonomous organizational fleets.

sources.title: Matthew Green: Is sandboxing sufficient to contain rogue agents?

title: Gemini 4 Argon
description: Google DeepMind's next-era frontier foundation model, delivering industry-leading performance across complex coding, defensive cybersecurity, and enterprise knowledge domains.
capabilityNote: Ranked by independent benchmarks as Google's definitive return to the top three labs by intelligence achieved.

sources.title: Google: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence

title: Clef (Cloudflare)
description: Cloudflare's open-source decision models (Clef and Clef-flash) hosted on Workers AI, providing fast, deterministic, calibrated decision routing for agentic workflows.
capabilityNote: Took top rank on the Jev Decision Index benchmark upon release, validating compact decision-specialized networks against broad generalist LLMs.

sources.title: Cloudflare: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models

title: Micron AI memory supply warning
description: Micron's executive leadership warned that hyperscaler AI infrastructure demands will drive severe DRAM and HBM memory shortages across 2027 and 2028.
capabilityNote: Highlighted memory bandwidth and supply allocation as the primary physical bottlenecks constraining frontier model scale beyond raw compute.

sources.title: TechPowerUp: Micron CEO Says Memory Supply Will Be Much Tighter in 2027-2028

title: PrismML Bonsai 27B
description: A 27B-parameter model compressed to ternary and 1-bit weights so it runs on a laptop (5.9 GB) or phone (3.9 GB). Bonsai 2 followed in September 2026 at 1.76 effective bits per weight.
capabilityNote: PrismML reports Bonsai 2 27B keeps 98.2% of its full-precision benchmark score at over 9x smaller; vendor figures, not independently reproduced.

title: Large AI models are cultural and social technologies
description: Science essay arguing large models are best understood like markets, bureaucracies and print: systems that summarise and reorganise human knowledge, not emerging minds.

sources.title: Science: Large AI models are cultural and social technologies

title: Hassabis: A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age
description: Hassabis proposes a US standards body, modelled on FINRA, to run voluntary pre-release tests of frontier models for cyber, bio and deception risks.

sources.title: DeepMind Institute: A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age

title: Hugging Face upskill
description: CLI that has a large model write an agent skill, then tests whether smaller models do better with it. Demonstrated by having Claude teach open models to write CUDA kernels.

sources.title: Hugging Face: We got Claude to teach open models how to write CUDA kernels

title: Prompt engineering
description: GPT-3 showed a model could be steered by examples written in its prompt, with no retraining. Crafting those prompts became a skill and then a job title.

title: Context engineering
description: Shopify's Tobi Lütke named the shift from wording one prompt to supplying everything the model needs to solve the task. Karpathy endorsed the term a week later.

sources.title: Addy Osmani: Context Engineering, Bringing Engineering Discipline to Prompts

title: Harness engineering
description: OpenAI described building a product of about a million lines with Codex agents and no hand-written source, by engineering the constraints, tools and checks around the agents.

title: Loop engineering
description: Osmani named the practice of designing the loop that prompts, verifies, retries and stops a coding agent, instead of typing each prompt yourself.

sources.title: ADTmag: Loop Engineering Emerges as Developers Put AI Coding Agents on Repeat

title: Graph engineering
description: Designing many agents as an explicit graph: nodes own a task, edges decide what runs next, shared state and verification gate the result. A move away from free-form multi-agent chat.

sources.title: CIO: Graph engineering is where AI agents stop working alone
Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents

title: Grok 4.7
description: xAI's flagship model for coding and knowledge work, with a 500K-token context window, text and image input, and adjustable reasoning effort.

sources.title: Lindy: Grok 4.7, pricing and what changed from 4.6

majorUpdates.title: Repository upload disabled
majorUpdates.summary: Users found the agent uploading whole directories to xAI-run cloud servers without clear consent, exposing files such as keys and passwords. xAI disabled the upload and said it would delete the data.

majorUpdates.title: Open-sourced under Apache 2.0
majorUpdates.summary: xAI published the Rust source for the agent loop, tools, terminal UI and extension system.

title: Grok Build
description: xAI's terminal coding agent, written in Rust. It entered beta in May 2026, became open source under Apache 2.0 in July, and calls xAI's proprietary Grok models.

sources.title: The Decoder: xAI open-sources Grok Build
Pulse 2: Grok Build launches early beta

title: Grok Bot
description: xAI's agent product: each bot gets its own cloud computer, signs in to your work apps, and runs multi-step and recurring tasks, pausing for approval when judgment is needed.
capabilityNote: It started as a beta bundled with SuperGrok Heavy and Cursor's top plans, then widened to all SuperGrok plans.

sources.title: Reworked: xAI wants in on the enterprise with Grok Bot
AI Builder Club: Grok Bot pricing

title: Emergent
description: A vibe-coding platform where autonomous agents build full-stack web and mobile apps from a description, aimed at small businesses and first-time builders.
capabilityNote: The company claims $50 million in annual recurring revenue and over 5 million users; these are its own figures.

majorUpdates.title: $70M raise at a $300M valuation
majorUpdates.summary: Led by SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 and Khosla Ventures.

sources.title: Business Wire: Emergent announces $23M and launches its vibe coding platform

title: Base44
description: An AI app builder that turns a description into a working app with a managed backend, database, sign-in and hosting included. Wix bought it for about $80 million in June 2025, when it was six months old.

majorUpdates.title: Acquired by Wix
majorUpdates.summary: About $80 million in cash up front, with earn-outs through 2029; Base44 stays a standalone product.

sources.title: The AI Insider: Wix acquires six-month-old Base44 for $80M cash

title: Agent Reach
description: A free command-line tool that gives agents read and search access to the web and to X, Reddit, YouTube, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, GitHub and RSS, by routing to existing CLIs such as yt-dlp. Sites that need a login need your credentials, and the README advises a small account because of blocking risk.
capabilityNote: Reaches about ten platforms and works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Cursor and Windsurf. Adoption evidence beyond stars is forks and issues, not independent usage reports.

title: Claude Managed Agents
description: A hosted agent harness behind an API. You define the model, prompt, tools, MCP servers and skills; Anthropic runs the agent in a managed cloud sandbox, or in one you host, for long-running and scheduled work.
capabilityNote: Sessions keep their files and history server-side, which makes them ineligible for Zero Data Retention or a HIPAA BAA while in beta.

sources.title: Winbuzzer: Anthropic launches Claude Managed Agents

title: SWE-agent
description: A research agent that takes a GitHub issue and tries to fix it with the language model of your choice. It reports state-of-the-art SWE-bench results among open-source projects, and is now in maintenance mode; the maintainers point to mini-swe-agent.

title: Open SWE
description: An open-source asynchronous coding agent from LangChain. It investigates a codebase, implements changes, validates them and delivers a pull request, from GitHub, Slack or Linear, in cloud sandboxes.

title: Kilo Code
description: An open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the CLI, with a cloud agent and 500+ models at provider prices with no markup.

title: Qwen Code
description: An open-source terminal coding agent from the Qwen team. It works with many model providers and local models, and runs in the terminal, desktop and web apps, IDE plugins and chat apps.

title: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini models, with a free daily allowance, MCP support, headless mode and a GitHub Action.

title: Plandex
description: An open-source coding agent built for large projects, with a diff-review sandbox and a 2M-token effective context. Its hosted cloud has been winding down since October 2025, and the last code push was the same month.

title: gptme
description: A terminal agent with local tools (shell, files, browser, computer use) that you can build into a persistent, scheduled agent on your own machine.

title: Open Interpreter
description: Started as a way to let a model run code on your computer; now a coding agent tuned for low-cost open models such as Kimi and DeepSeek, with a terminal UI, ACP editors and desktop clients.

title: Stagehand
description: An SDK for browser agents, in TypeScript, Python and Go, with act, observe and extract calls, self-healing when sites change, and an MCP server.

title: Skyvern
description: Browser automation that uses vision models instead of brittle selectors, with workflows, 2FA and password-manager support. Self-host it or use the paid cloud.

title: Bytebot
description: A self-hosted AI desktop agent that works in a containerised Linux desktop, with a takeover mode. The repository was archived in March 2026.

title: UI-TARS Desktop
description: ByteDance's open-source GUI agent for your local computer, driven by UI-TARS vision models, alongside Agent TARS, a multimodal agent stack for terminal, computer and browser control.

title: Amp
description: A coding agent for the terminal and editors, spun out of Sourcegraph as Amp, Inc. in December 2025. It routes between models automatically. Its free tier moved from ads to a daily credit and was paused by mid-2026.

title: Deep Agents
description: LangChain's opinionated agent harness, built on LangGraph, with planning, sub-agents, a filesystem, skills, persistent memory, sandboxed shell access and human approval out of the box.

title: E2B
description: Open-source infrastructure for running AI-generated code in isolated cloud sandboxes, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, a desktop SDK for mouse and keyboard control, and Terraform-based self-hosting.

title: Daytona
description: Sandbox infrastructure for running AI-generated code, with sub-90ms start-up claimed. The public repository was archived in 2026 and says development moved to a private codebase.

title: Langfuse
description: Open-source LLM observability: tracing, evals, prompt management and datasets. MIT except its enterprise folders; part of ClickHouse since January 2026.

title: Arize Phoenix
description: OpenTelemetry-based tracing, evals, datasets and prompt tools for LLM apps, with a remote MCP server. Licensed under Elastic License 2.0, which is source-available rather than open source.

title: LiteLLM
description: An SDK and gateway that puts 100+ model providers behind one API, with spend tracking, virtual keys, fallbacks, guardrails and an MCP gateway.

title: Qdrant
description: A vector database written in Rust, with dense, sparse and multi-vector search, rich filtering, quantization, sharding and a managed cloud with a free tier.

title: Weaviate
description: A vector database written in Go, with hybrid search, built-in vectorizer modules, multi-tenancy and generative search. The community edition is BSD-3; an enterprise edition needs a commercial licence.

title: Milvus
description: A vector database with Lite, Standalone and Kubernetes-distributed modes, hybrid dense and sparse search, GPU indexes, and a managed cloud, Zilliz Cloud.

title: LightRAG
description: A graph-based retrieval framework positioned as a lighter alternative to Microsoft GraphRAG, with a web UI, REST API and many storage backends.

title: GraphRAG
description: Microsoft's pipeline that uses an LLM to build a knowledge graph from text for retrieval. It is demonstration code in maintenance mode, not an officially supported product, and indexing can be expensive.

title: RAGFlow
description: An open-source retrieval engine with deep document parsing (layout, OCR, tables), agentic retrieval and a web UI.

title: GPT Researcher
description: An autonomous research agent that produces cited reports of 2,000+ words from the web, MCP sources and your own documents. The project claims about $0.40 per deep-research run.

title: STORM
description: Stanford's system that writes Wikipedia-style articles with citations from internet search, with Co-STORM for working alongside a person. The last code push was September 2025.

title: LiveKit Agents
description: A framework for realtime voice and video agents, with mix-and-match speech, language and voice providers, semantic turn detection, telephony and MCP.

title: Pipecat
description: A Python framework for realtime voice and multimodal agents, with 20+ providers per stage, WebRTC and WebSocket transports, and telephony.

title: WebArena
description: A self-hostable benchmark of 812 realistic web tasks (shopping, Reddit, GitLab, Wikipedia) for testing autonomous agents. The 2023 paper compares agents with human annotators.

title: BrowserGym
description: A Gym environment for web agents that bundles benchmarks including MiniWoB, WebArena, VisualWebArena and WorkArena.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
description: Anthropic's small, fast model, priced at $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million tokens. It is available on every Claude plan including Free, on the major clouds, and in Claude Code.
capabilityNote: Anthropic says it is a significant step up from Haiku 4.5 across coding, tool use, computer use and agents, and reports 92.8% on a HubSpot CRM task suite; vendor figures.

title: Claude Opus 5.5
description: Anthropic's flagship Opus model, priced at $4 in and $20 out per million tokens against $5 and $25 for Opus 5, with output more than 30% faster.

sources.title: BetaNews: Claude Opus 5.5 launch price cut

title: Mistral Large 4
description: Mistral's 1.05-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, 52B active per token, with a 1M-token context window and image input. It launched as a public preview on 6 October; open weights followed on Hugging Face under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License.

sources.title: mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B on Hugging Face (model card, licence)
byteiota: Mistral Large 4, open weights with a catch

capabilityNote: The licence is a modified MIT: commercial and non-commercial use are allowed, but running a Model-as-a-Service business needs a separate commercial licence from Mistral. Earlier Mistral flagships used Apache 2.0.

title: Nano Banana 2.1
description: Google's image generation and editing model on Gemini 3.6 Flash, generally available at about half the per-image price of Nano Banana 2, across the Gemini app, Search AI Mode, AI Studio and the API. Nano Banana 2 is scheduled to shut down on 29 October 2026.

sources.title: Unite.AI: Nano Banana 2.1 halves the image price

title: ChatGPT Intelligent UI and GPT-6
description: OpenAI began rolling GPT-6 into ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, which answers with interactive charts, forms, buttons and editable diagrams instead of plain text. Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise got GPT-6 Sol first; Free and Go followed on 8 October with GPT-6 Luna.

sources.title: OpenAI: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
Unite.AI: GPT-6 with Intelligent UI to all ChatGPT tiers

title: Harness acquires Augment Code's Cosmos and Auggie
description: Harness bought selected Augment Code assets: Cosmos, the Auggie CLI, the Code Context Engine and the team. Cosmos becomes the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent, which coordinates agents from a ticket or bug through code, tests and a pull request, and keeps working when review comments or checks fail. The price was not disclosed.

sources.title: Unite.AI: Harness acquires Augment Code assets

title: IBM Bob
description: IBM's AI software-development partner for enterprises, generally available as SaaS with a 30-day trial and individual and enterprise plans. On 1 October 2026 IBM added self-hosted deployment for on-premises, private-cloud, sovereign-cloud and air-gapped environments.

majorUpdates.title: Self-hosted deployment
majorUpdates.summary: Run Bob on-premises, in private or sovereign clouds, or fully air-gapped.

sources.title: IBM Newsroom: self-hosted deployment for IBM Bob

title: Muse Code
description: Meta's coding agent, in preview from August 2026. It plans changes, writes code and validates results end to end, powered by Muse Spark 1.2, at $1.25 in and $4.25 out per million tokens, with a discounted tier for developers who share improvement data.

sources.title: DevOps.com: Meta launches AI coding agent

title: Claude-Mem
description: A memory layer that records what your coding agent does in a session, compresses it with AI, and feeds the relevant parts back into later sessions. Local-first, with a SQLite and Chroma store and search tools over MCP; works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Hermes and others.
capabilityNote: Compression and recall use a model, so the memory feature draws on your existing plan unless you subscribe to its optional cloud sync.

title: nanobot
description: An ultra-lightweight, self-hosted personal agent framework in Python, with a web UI, MCP, long-term memory, sub-agents, cron automation and chat apps including Telegram, Discord, Slack and WeChat.

title: CowAgent
description: An open-source personal assistant and agent harness that started as chatgpt-on-wechat. It now plans tasks, runs tools and skills, keeps a three-tier memory, and supports multi-agent teams, MCP, browser control and chat channels such as WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram and Slack.
capabilityNote: The 2022 date is the repository's creation as a ChatGPT-on-WeChat bot; the agent features came much later.

title: ECC (Everything Claude Code)
description: A harness-optimisation toolkit for Claude Code, Codex and other agents: 68 agents, 293 skills, 94 commands, rules, hooks, a portable memory vault and AgentShield, a scanner for prompts, hooks and MCP config. A paid ECC Pro GitHub App covers private repos.
capabilityNote: Most of its bulk is skills and prompts rather than a new runtime; its star count measures attention, not use.

title: Ruflo
description: An orchestration layer for Claude Code and Codex that adds swarms of specialised agents, vector memory, hooks, an MCP server and a terminal console. It began as Claude Flow and was renamed Ruflo.
capabilityNote: The README counts 98 agents, 30 skills and 35 plugins on the full install. Its own download counter is labelled illustrative, so treat usage figures as the author's, not independent.

title: LM Studio
description: A desktop app for downloading and running open-weight models on your own machine, with a chat window and an OpenAI-compatible local server. Closed source, free to use.
capabilityNote: Added Apple MLX support in Oct 2024 and later headless operation. Its 0.4.x line shipped through 2026. Third-party sources date the first release to May 2023.

title: LM Studio Bionic
description: A separate agent app from the LM Studio team for coding, research and work on documents and files, running open models locally or on LM Studio's hosted cloud.
capabilityNote: Launched for Mac and Windows; its changelog later lists Linux builds (1.1.2, Sep 2026). Cloud models bill pay-as-you-go credits; running local models is free.

title: Claude Code mods
description: A kind of Claude Code plugin whose JavaScript or TypeScript event handlers run inside Claude Code itself, so they can draw panes, add commands and intercept tool calls and prompts.
capabilityNote: Not sandboxed: a mod runs with your account's permissions and can read files and secrets. Needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later; admins can restrict them through managed settings.

title: DeepInfer
description: DeepSeek's inference engine, open-sourced for offline inference of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. It includes speculative decoding, batch-invariant inference, deterministic sampling and structured outputs.
capabilityNote: A partial release: the README says the KV cache system, which a complete serving stack needs, is not included.
